name: QOBLIB exact assignment lotteries: beat 14 terms for B5_25_2 or 20 for B6_36_10
compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days for search; exact checking takes seconds; 5x5 and 6x6 integer matrices, respectively 120 and 720 possible permutation columns
statement: QOBLIB’s Minimum Birkhoff Decomposition problem minimizes the number of permutation matrices in an exact convex decomposition of a doubly stochastic matrix. On 2026-10-24 its table lists B5_25_2 at 14 and B6_36_10 at 20, both best known. The source credits J. Kulkarni, E. Lee and M. Singh (2017), and F. Dufossé and B. Uçar (2016). Maximilian Schicker’s submissions dated 2026-01-10 give integer-weight-model numerical lower bounds 13 and 11, not exact unrestricted lower bounds. Both target matrices have scale 10000 in qbench_05_dense.json and qbench_06_dense.json. Independent exact arithmetic confirms the 14/20-term MIP witnesses. The current .bst.json files have 13/17 terms, but neither support can reconstruct its target over rational weights, in either orientation. Their approximate counts therefore do not settle these exact targets.
success_criterion: For either named matrix A, give pairwise distinct permutations and strictly positive rational weights w_k summing to 10000 such that A=sum_k w_k P_k entrywise exactly, with at most 13 terms for B5_25_2 or at most 19 for B6_36_10. This is a record win; global minimality need not be proved. Also strictly improve the best comparable published result at claim time, including compatible compositions of published objects. State whether the candidate is a composition and identify its components. Values in unmerged pull requests do not set the bar. Alternatively, close either exact optimum by an attaining decomposition and an independently checkable lower-bound certificate valid for arbitrary nonnegative real weights. A certificate restricted to integer weights does not establish the latter claim.
verification_method: Locate instances by their id, not JSON insertion order. Check integer matrix entries, common row/column sum 10000 and each submitted permutation of 1..n. Merge duplicate permutations and discard zero weights before counting. Clear rational denominators and check all 25 or 36 reconstruction equations and the weight sum with arbitrary-precision integers; tolerance must be zero. Use row-major storage, as confirmed against the exact MIP incumbents. For an optimality claim, a rational MILP branch proof over all n! support indicators and continuous weights can be checked node by node using Farkas/dual certificates. The small audit script checks fixed supports, not optimality, and is not a substitute for a general lower-bound proof.
status_checked: 2026-10-24 (live table, exact incumbent witnesses and inconsistent approximate supports independently checked)
angles: Start with a support-selection MILP over 120 or 720 permutations, then solve its weights exactly. Integer-only models are useful for finding witnesses but restrict the mathematical problem.
Use the approximate 13/17-term supports only as search seeds. They cannot be made exact just by increasing numerical precision; their exact systems are inconsistent.
Favor local support replacement and exact nullspace reductions. Keep all matrix equations, not only row and column totals.
pitfalls: The instance description and checker use different storage-language conventions; these MIP witnesses reconstruct the target in row-major order.
A smaller approximate support is not an exact decomposition.
The reported lower bounds use an integer-weight model and numerical solving.
Exact rational weights, including any strict improvement, require zero reconstruction tolerance.
The solver table requires commit-only disclosure for a new candidate; published incumbent data can be cited.
